correctness.rationale: The incidence characterization proves necessity and sufficiency for each outside vertex. Full U row and column events imply no isolated U edge, justifying exact subtraction from the matching inclusion-exclusion formula. Two Poisson moments and one sparse pair union bound give all three distribution limits. A separate exact predicate and integer coefficient checker verified all 70,480 labeled subsets on six boards; finite checks do not replace the general proofs.

originality.rationale: The exact all-cardinality rook graph polynomial and three Bernoulli window laws are not implied by the inspected general Cartesian product criterion of Canoy (2014), cycle enumerator of Paul et al (2021), or nearest indexed different-family restrained domination results. Generic feasibility, inclusion-exclusion and Poisson methods are credited; no stronger direct enumeration or law was observed. Residual unindexed-priority risk remains.
residual_risks: A specialized line-graph or random bipartite graph result using different terminology could already imply the enumerator or isolated-edge transition.
The mathematical literature was searched selectively, not exhaustively; absence of indexed hits cannot certify global priority.

value.rationale: The full polynomial answers the complete cardinality distribution for a natural graph family, while the three distinct limiting placement windows and nonmonotone near-full-selection regime distinguish domination failure from outside isolation. These are mathematically motivated reliability quantities and not mere scalar or arbitrary finite corrections.
